$comment: Written reasons for the capabilities catalogue (docs/DSL_CAPABILITIES.html), batch 4 of N, 2026-11-23 (REG-357, owner: do only 20% of the remaining cases, of mixed complexity). One reason per keyword: what need it serves and why a lower rung of the extension ladder (expression, function, flow step, hand-written code) or an existing keyword cannot do it. The reasons state the need, not the evidence counts: the catalogue's own columns show samples, tests and examples and change as the corpus grows, so a count written here would go stale. The batch is every 5th keyword still without a reason, taken within each kind of value (boolean, text, number, choice, list, object, reference) so simple and complex ones are mixed. Key = slot id exactly as the catalogue shows it; the generator refuses a reason for a keyword the schema does not have.

reasons.actionMetadata.permissionHint: A greyed-out Approve button should tell the clerk why; the hint names the permission the action needs, as text shown to a person, and there is no logic behind it for an expression or a flow to replace.
reasons.aggregateBalance.name: When a bill's lines do not add up to its total, the error the person sees must name the rule that failed; the balance rule's name is that identifier, required and unique inside the aggregate so two rules can never produce the same message.
reasons.aggregateCollection.ownership: An order's lines belong to the order and disappear with it, but an order's tags are shared with other orders and must survive; the choice between owned and referenced tells the platform whether to create and delete the child rows or only link them, which no expression can decide after the fact.
reasons.aggregateCollectionLookupField.query: A line's product picker should offer the products of a query that loads once with the collection; naming the declared query keeps the options on the same governed read path instead of copying product data into the model.
reasons.agentAccessExposure.confirmWrites: A chat assistant could delete a record or start a refund on a misread sentence; asking for a yes before any create, update, delete or flow run puts a person back in the loop, and it has to be a platform setting because the confirmation is shown in the channel, which no flow or expression reaches.
reasons.agentAccessExposure.fields: A support assistant should see a customer's name and city but not the internal notes; an allow-list narrows what the agent sees and may set, and a sensitive field stays hidden even if someone lists it, so a slip in the list cannot leak it.
reasons.autoPanel.aggregate: To open an order together with its lines on one screen, the generated panel must know which concept is the root; naming the aggregate root turns the panel into the aggregate workbench, a choice of structure rather than a value an expression could compute.
reasons.autoPanel.detail: The page that shows one customer often needs settings of its own, apart from the list of customers; a detail block holds them so the single-record surface can differ from the list without a hand-made page.
reasons.autoPanel.metadata: A team may want to carry its own note on a generated screen, such as an owner or a ticket reference, into the compiled model without the platform acting on it; free-form metadata is that place, where a comment in the JSON would be lost on compile.
reasons.autoPanelSurface.fields: A staff list may need only five of a concept's twenty fields, in a chosen order; naming the fields per surface keeps the generated screen narrow without a hand-made page, where the default would show everything.
reasons.capabilityContractSchemaRef.conceptRef: A capability that returns a customer should say its result has the shape of the Customer concept instead of describing the fields a second time; pointing at the concept reuses one shape and follows it when it changes.
reasons.capabilityOperation.http: A capability backed by a web service must say which request to make, its method, path and body; the http block holds that, so an integration is a declaration and not hand-written code until the call needs real logic.
reasons.capabilityOperation.output: A capability that looks up a tax rate must say what it returns, so callers and the validator know the type of the answer; the output type is the contract, written in the same forms as the input, and no step can state it.
reasons.capabilityPolicy.circuitOpenAfterFailure: When a payment provider is down, ten customers should not each wait for a timeout; opening the circuit after a number of consecutive failures makes later calls fail fast and protects the rest of the app, a behavior around every call that no flow step can provide from inside one call.
reasons.cellGrid.rowsField: A seating plan or warehouse board with a different number of rows for each layout can keep that count on the record; naming the integer field lets the board read its row count from data instead of a number typed into the model.
reasons.concept.rollups: A post's like count should always equal the number of Like rows pointing at it, even when two people tap at once; a stored field the platform recomputes inside every child save or delete stays true for every door, where a flow or a hand-run function could be skipped by one of them and drift.
reasons.conceptAccess.public: A restaurant menu or a public price list is for people who have no account; an anonymous read-only grant, with a where saying which rows are public, opens reading only through the public surface and never writes, so nothing is exposed by a forgotten role.
reasons.context.name: In a model split into areas such as billing and sales, each area needs a name that prefixes its members, so two areas can each have a concept called Invoice without a clash; the name is the namespace, and no expression can create one.
reasons.conversionCaseWhen.then: When old data is converted, the old code A must become ACTIVE; each case writes its literal value, so the conversion is a readable table of cases and no code runs on live data.
reasons.domainType.name: A Phone or Money type defined once and reused by many fields needs a name to be referenced by; the name is what a field's domainType points at, so a rule changes in one place instead of on every field.
reasons.domainType.ui: Every phone field in an app should look the same, with the same mask and hint; presentation hints set on the domain type are inherited by every field of that type, where setting them field by field would drift.
reasons.event.version: When the shape of an OrderPlaced event changes, listeners built for the old shape must still know what they are receiving; a version label on the payload contract says which one it is, and a flow step has no place to carry a contract label.
reasons.eventPayloadField.type: An event telling the warehouse that twelve pallets arrived must carry a number, not text, or every listener has to guess; typing each payload field makes the event a contract that consumers and the validator can trust.
reasons.externalAi.vendors: A company may allow a document summarizer to talk to one AI vendor and not to another; listing the allowed vendor ids writes that choice into the model, so the app cannot quietly send data to a provider nobody approved.
reasons.field.maxLength: A product code printed on a label must not exceed twelve characters; stating the limit on the field makes every screen, import and API refuse a longer value, and a check written into each flow would miss the doors that do not run it.
reasons.field.unique: Two customers must not share one email or one tax number; saying so on the field makes the platform refuse the duplicate however the row arrives, screen, import, API or flow, and it respects the tenant and soft-deleted rows, which a check written into one flow would not.
reasons.flow.concept: Most steps of a flow work on one concept, such as Order; naming it once spares writing it on every step, and a step that needs another concept still says so with its own scope.
reasons.flowStep.awaitRef: When a flow waits for a customer's reply, the reply's data must be kept where later steps can read it; the awaitRef names that place in the flow state, so the next step can use the answer.
reasons.flowStep.input: A step that creates or updates a record must be handed the data; the input says what is handed over, a flow-state reference or an expression, and for a concept step it is the record body. No other keyword says what a step receives.
reasons.flowStep.match: A flow waiting for payment received must pick the right payment among many that arrive; the match says how an arriving event is tied to this waiting instance, a rule that belongs to the waiting step itself and that an expression elsewhere cannot supply.
reasons.flowStep.then: A refund over a limit goes to a manager and any other is paid at once; the then list holds the steps of the true side of a branch, so both paths read in order, which one expression cannot do because a path is a series of steps and not a value.
reasons.guidePage.name: A concept or screen that wants to open its own help page needs something to point at; the page's name is that handle, so the link survives a change of the page's title.
reasons.guidePageRegion.width: On a wide page a side column of notes may take a quarter of the width and the main text the rest; a width per region sets that layout directly, a pure presentation choice with no lower rung.
reasons.guidePageRegions.top: A help page may want a banner above the content, or none; a switch per region lets each page show or hide its top strip without a different page template, and page structure is not something an expression can express.
reasons.guidePageTheme.density: A help page for a busy warehouse worker may want tight spacing and one for a new customer airy spacing; a density setting changes the spacing of the whole page at once, a presentation choice only.
reasons.httpConnector.headers: A partner API that wants the same fixed header on every call is served by declaring the headers once on the connector, instead of repeating them on each operation.
reasons.httpConnectorOperation.body: A partner API that expects a JSON object with the order number and the total is described by a template filled from the call's parameters, so the operation needs no code; it is ignored for GET and DELETE, which have no body.
reasons.httpConnectorOperation.bodyEncoding: Some partner APIs want a JSON body and older ones a classic web form; choosing the encoding on the operation lets the same kind of capability talk to both, where writing it by hand would need code for each connector.
reasons.httpConnectorOperation.path: Calling a partner at a path such as /orders/{orderId} needs the path of the request and the place where the id goes; the placeholders are filled from the call's parameters, so one operation serves every order without code that builds strings.
reasons.lifecycle.statusField: An order's state needs a field to live in; naming the enum field that stores it lets the lifecycle sit on a concept that already calls that field phase, while the default name status suits most.
reasons.lifecycleState.allowedActions: A shipped order should offer track and return but not edit address; listing the actions per state makes the buttons follow the lifecycle, where a condition repeated on every button of every screen would drift from the rules.
reasons.lifecycleTransition.actionLabel: The button that moves an order from paid to shipped should say Ship order in the user's words, not the name of a state; the caption on the transition carries it where the transition is defined, so every screen shows the same words.
reasons.pack:author: Someone installing a pack wants to know who stands behind it; a free-text author line is shown with the pack, and it is attribution only, with no logic for anything else to replace.
reasons.pack:deprecated: A pack author who finds a flaw in version 1.2 wants everyone to move on; marking that version deprecated inside the version itself, before it is published, keeps published versions immutable, where a later edit would change content people already installed.
reasons.pack:imports: A billing context that refers to a customer in the sales context must say so; listing the contexts it may reference turns a typo or an unplanned dependency into a compile error and not a silent miss, and no flow or function can guard something resolved at compile time.
reasons.panelAction.concept: A button that creates or edits a record must know which kind of record; for a concept binding the concept names it, because the binding alone has nothing to act on.
reasons.panelAction.inputFields: A reassign ticket button must ask who should get the ticket before it runs; naming the fields to collect makes the screen show a small form and hand the answers to the flow as its input, which saves a hand-written dialog.
reasons.panelAction.visibleWhen: A Cancel order button should only appear while the order can still be cancelled; the expression language already says when, and this keyword is the place where the screen asks it, so the button follows the data without a second page.
reasons.panelFieldBinding.readonlyWhen: A price field should be editable only while the order is a draft; the expression language says when, and this keyword is where the field asks it, so the screen needs no second form for the locked state.
reasons.panelSlot.placement: A custom block such as a map must sometimes sit above the generated table, sometimes below it and sometimes take its place; the placement says which, and replace is limited to one per panel so two blocks cannot fight for the same spot. Page structure is not something an expression can express.
reasons.panelWidget.filter: A dashboard tile that counts only the open tickets needs rows whose status equals open; a simple equality filter on the widget aggregates just those rows, short of declaring and naming a separate query for every tile.
reasons.panelWidget.title: A dashboard tile needs a heading such as Open tickets; the title is the text above the number, shown to people, with no logic behind it.
reasons.presentationMetadata.placeholder: An empty phone input is clearer when it shows an example number; the placeholder is hint text inside an empty input, shown to the user, with no logic behind it.
reasons.presentationMetadata.selectionTools: Someone reviewing forty invoices wants to tick a few and open them together or paste them into a spreadsheet; the three tools on ticked rows are behavior of the generated grid, switched on or off per concept, and no flow or function can add buttons to a generated grid.
reasons.propertyScope.from: A setting such as currency may be overridden per tenant or per user; from says where this level's id comes from at sign-in, so the platform can pick the right value for each request without a hand-written lookup.
reasons.query.computed: A shopping list needs to buy equal to needed minus owned on every row; computed columns derived per group from grouped, aggregate and lookup columns give report numbers inside the query itself, where a flow would have to fetch the rows and loop over them.
reasons.queryLookup.where: A lookup column that shows only the active price list for a product needs a filter on the lookup concept's rows; where uses the same grammar as the query's own filter, so one filter language serves both.
reasons.referenceDefinition.via: A line that points at a product by its barcode instead of its internal id needs to say which field of the target to use; via names it, and it must be the target's id or a unique anchor field, so the link stays unambiguous.
reasons.role.grants: A clerk role should never be able to run administration actions, however it is set up later; declaring the platform permissions the role may hold is a ceiling the validator checks, and a flow or expression cannot enforce it because it is about who is allowed to ask.
reasons.root:modules: A large app, such as a clinic with scheduling, billing and pharmacy, is easier to keep as separate areas each in its own file; module declarations name each area and point at its fragment, using the composition packs and fragments already use, and plain code cannot split a model file.
reasons.schemaObject.duplicationPolicy: A list of phone numbers or ingredients can repeat one by mistake; saying whether elements that share the same identity are allowed or refused makes the platform check every list on save, where a flow would have to loop and compare for each list in the model.
reasons.schemaObject.enumValues: A shipping speed in an extension's data shape must be one of a few words; listing the allowed values lets the platform refuse anything else uniformly, where free text with a check in code would be done differently each time.
reasons.schemaObject.items: A list of addresses in a data shape must say what one address looks like; items describes every element, so the platform checks each one, and a shape is a declaration that no expression can stand in for.
reasons.schemaObject.max: A data shape says a rating can be at most 5; the platform enforces the largest allowed value wherever that shape is used, where a check in code would have to be repeated at each place.
reasons.schemaObject.regex: A product code must look like two letters and four digits; a regular expression on a string value makes the platform refuse anything else wherever the shape is used.
reasons.transactionHooks.onFieldChange: When a user edits a cell of a draft order, other cells such as the total should update at once; the hook runs on every cell edit, debounced, and the state it returns patches the draft. That has to happen between keystrokes and the server, which a later flow cannot do.
reasons.workbenchActionApplyTo.map: After a workbench action runs a flow, the result must land in the right fields of the row, such as a storage location returned by the flow going to the line's location field; a map from target field to a path in the flow result says where each piece goes, as data the platform can check.
